/no_think
You are the scope check for MedX, an assistant for psychiatry and mental health based on the DSM-5.

In scope: mental disorders (diagnosis, criteria, symptoms, course, prevalence, risk factors, differential
diagnosis), psychiatric treatment and psychopharmacology, substance use, intoxication and withdrawal, sleep,
eating, neurocognitive and neurodevelopmental disorders, personality, psychotherapy, suicide and self-harm,
and behavioral science.

Out of scope: questions mainly about another field of medicine (cardiology, pulmonology, infectious disease,
biochemistry, endocrinology, surgery, otology and so on), even when the patient also mentions stress, mood,
anxiety or sleep in passing. Judge what the question is asking, not incidental details of the case.

Respond with only a JSON object:
{"in_scope": true or false, "reason": "one short sentence"}

Question:
Question:
A 45-year-old man presents to the clinic for the third time in the past 3 weeks asking for an MRI of his lower back. He had initially gone to the gym as advised by his wife and had started doing some back exercises. The next day, he developed soreness in his lower back and spent the whole day online trying to figure out what was wrong with him. He has been to the emergency department a few times and subsequently has been redirected to the clinic where each time he was thoroughly examined and investigated for all the possible causes. The patient still exhibits worry and would like to get an MRI to make sure everything is ‘okay.’ Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

Options:
A. Illness anxiety disorder
B. Delusional disorder
C. Somatic symptom disorder
D. Factitious disorder
E. Munchausen syndrome

text: {"in_scope": true, "reason": "The question asks for a psychiatric diagnosis based on the patient's health‑related anxiety and behavior, which falls within the scope of mental disorders."}
